humanizer.name: humanizer
humanizer.invocation: Humanizer 2.2.0 full-batch pattern scan, read-aloud pass, anti-AI pass, and writing.md checklist for the docs/08 stat, perk and grade strings, re-run when the roster went whole-game.

rewrites.before: Lifting, running, moving the body.
rewrites.after: Lifting, running, carrying things.
rewrites.reason: "Moving the body" is clinical where the other three name real activities; a concrete third item reads as a person rather than a stat block.

rewrites.before: Hands, cooking, the fine work.
rewrites.after: Cooking, and anything fiddly.
rewrites.reason: Rule of three with a vague third item. One concrete noun plus one plain adjective says the same in fewer words.

rewrites.before: How well the body takes care.
rewrites.after: Getting the most out of rest and a wash.
rewrites.reason: The original is not quite grammatical and hides the mechanic. The rewrite names the two activities the stat actually governs.

rewrites.before: Attention, learning, practice.
rewrites.after: Focus, and how much practice sticks.
rewrites.reason: Three bare abstract nouns is the flattest AI cadence in the file. "Sticks" is the word a person would use for retention.

rewrites.before: Better and slower at the expressive things.
rewrites.after: Takes longer over cooking and practice, and does them better.
rewrites.reason: "The expressive things" leaks the internal tag name. Naming the activities makes the trade legible without the player learning our vocabulary.

rewrites.before: Better and slower at the routine things.
rewrites.after: Takes longer over the daily upkeep, and does it better.
rewrites.reason: Same tag leak as its pair, and "daily upkeep" is what the player already calls brushing and showering.

rewrites.before: Gets through the day quickly.
rewrites.after: Gets through the day faster.
rewrites.reason: Comparative, because the trait only means anything against the alternative Drive option.

rewrites.before: Reading people, and being read well by them.
rewrites.after: Reading a room, and being read well.
rewrites.reason: The original repeated "people"/"them" for one idea. "A room" is the concrete thing a busker actually reads, and it points at v2 without naming a system the player cannot see yet.

rewrites.before: Recharges alone, and spends that charge on people later.
rewrites.after: Recharges alone, and spends that on people later.
rewrites.reason: "That charge" restates the battery metaphor the sentence already carries. Cutting the noun keeps the rhythm and the meaning.

rewrites.before: Holds their nerve when the pressure is on.
rewrites.after: Holds their nerve when it counts.
rewrites.reason: "When the pressure is on" is an idiom doing no work next to "nerve". The shorter clause says the same and reads aloud better.

rewrites.before: No system uses this yet
rewrites.after: Nothing uses this yet
rewrites.reason: "System" is our word, not the player's. The line appears under a stat they can see a number for, so the plainer noun carries it.

reviews.checklist: Humanizer 2.2.0 and writing.md section 5 passed. Grade labels stay the bare letters so the letter remains the whole signal (docs/08 §11.5). Perk blurbs state the cost as well as the benefit, because every one of them is a trade. The dormant line is written for a player who can see the number and wonders why nothing moves it — it answers that, and does not apologise for it.
